feedback.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=2{x}^{2}y-4x{y}^{2}-x+6{y}^{3}.
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,0]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration. Round the answer for ${x}_{1}$ to **three decimal places**.

| $[$ | $0$ | {{field-1}} | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | {{field-2}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-3}} | $-8$ | $-2$ |  |  |  |

| ${x}_{1}=[$ | $1$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-4}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}y-4x{y}^{2}-x+6{y}^{3}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}y-4x{y}^{2}-x+6{y}^{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4xy-4{y}^{2}-1 \\ 2{x}^{2}-8xy+18{y}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(4xy-4{y}^{2}-1) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}-8xy+18{y}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(4xy-4{y}^{2}-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}-8xy+18{y}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4y & 4x-8y \\ 4x-8y & 36y-8x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}4y & 4x-8y \\ 4x-8y & 36y-8x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}4xy-4{y}^{2}-1 \\ 2{x}^{2}-8xy+18{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}4y & 4x-8y \\ 4x-8y & 36y-8x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}4xy-4{y}^{2}-1 \\ 2{x}^{2}-8xy+18{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}4(0) & 4(1)-8(0) \\ 4(1)-8(0) & 36(0)-8(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}4(1)(0)-4(0)^{2}-1 \\ 2(1)^{2}-8(1)(0)+18(0)^{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 4 & -8\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1/4\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0.25\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
